title: Profitability Ephemerality
claim: Trading profitability is ephemeral and requires continuous risk management; historical examples demonstrate over-estimated valuations and investor losses.

title: Supply-Demand Equilibrium and Price Discovery
claim: Modern markets are driven by supply-demand equilibrium; price discovery is fundamental to market operations. Increased technology and market participant access makes price discovery more efficient than historically.

title: Order Matching Algorithms
claim: Exchanges facilitate price discovery through order matching; matching algorithms (FIFO vs pro-rata) determine execution outcomes. Different order types (market, limit, iceberg, stop) route through matching engines with different priorities.

title: Algorithmic Trading Speed Risk
claim: Automated trading systems inherit market risk and operational risk; execution speed advantages can amplify losses when volatility spikes or systems malfunction.

title: Technical Indicator Fundamentals
claim: Technical indicators (SMA, EMA, RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands) extract trading signals from price/volume. Simple Moving Average (SMA) averages price over N periods. Exponential Moving Average (EMA) weights recent prices more heavily.

title: RSI and MACD Signal Lag
claim: RSI and MACD rely on historical price patterns; overbought/oversold signals can lag during trending markets. Bollinger Bands may generate false breakout signals when volatility regime changes abruptly.

title: ML Indicator Overfitting Risk
claim: Machine learning models trained on historical indicators risk overfitting to past regimes; forward testing and out-of-sample validation essential before deployment.

title: Supervised Learning Feature Engineering
claim: Supervised learning (classification, regression) predicts price movements from features (price, volume, indicators). Feature engineering critical; raw indicators may contain multicollinearity and redundancy.

title: Data Leakage in ML Backtesting
claim: Data leakage (using future information to train) invalidates backtests; proper temporal separation of train/validation/test sets required; walk-forward validation recommended.

title: Momentum Strategy Volatility Scaling
claim: Momentum strategies exploit price trends; buy assets with rising prices, sell with falling prices. Volatility adjustment improves risk-adjusted returns; scaling position size inversely with volatility stabilizes portfolio returns.

title: Mean-Reversion Pair Trading
claim: Mean-reversion strategies assume prices revert to historical average; identify overbought/oversold conditions. Pair trading exploits mean-reversion between correlated assets; requires mean-reversion regime detection.

title: Statistical Arbitrage Cointegration
claim: Statistical arbitrage exploits pricing inefficiencies between correlated securities. Cointegration testing identifies stationary price spreads; trading when spread deviates from historical mean.

title: Execution Algorithms TWAP VWAP
claim: Execution algorithms minimize transaction costs and market impact. TWAP (Time-Weighted Average Price) distributes order over time window. VWAP (Volume-Weighted Average Price) aligns execution with market volume profile.

title: Execution Slippage Cost Impact
claim: Execution slippage (actual fill price vs model price) can erode strategy profitability; simulated transaction costs in backtest must account for realistic market impact and latency effects.

title: Risk Quantification Sharpe Drawdown VaR
claim: Risk metrics: Sharpe Ratio (return per unit volatility), Maximum Drawdown (peak-to-trough decline), Value-at-Risk (VaR, worst-case loss percentile). Portfolio volatility computed from asset correlations; diversification reduces joint risk.

title: Real-Time Risk Controls Position Limits
claim: Live trading requires real-time risk limits: position limits (max notional, max contracts), drawdown stops, Greeks hedging (delta, gamma, theta for derivatives). Breach triggers automatic order cancellation or liquidation.

title: VaR Tail Risk Limitations
claim: VaR underestimates tail risk during market stress; fat-tailed distributions and regime changes exceed VaR thresholds. Stress testing and scenario analysis necessary complements to VaR.

title: Modular Trading System Architecture
claim: Modular trading system architecture: data ingestion (feeds, market data) → signal generation (strategy logic) → execution (order router) → settlement (risk reconciliation). Decoupling enables independent testing and deployment.

title: Order Management System Gateway
claim: Order Management System (OMS) gateway coordinates order lifecycle: creation, routing, execution, cancellation, settlement. Audit trail required for regulatory compliance. Idempotent order handling prevents duplicate fills.

title: FIX Protocol Message Sequencing
claim: FIX (Financial Information Exchange) protocol standard for order routing to exchanges. Message types: NewOrderSingle, ExecutionReport, OrderCancelRequest. Reliable delivery and message sequencing critical.

title: Market Data Feed Integration Multicast
claim: Market data feeds provide real-time price/volume updates. Multicast feeds (low-latency) vs unicast (reliable). Feed normalization and heartbeat monitoring required to detect gaps or exchange outages.

title: Backtesting Engine For-Loop vs Event-Driven
claim: Backtester options: for-loop model (fast, simplified) vs event-driven simulator (realistic, complex). Event-driven accommodates realistic order latency, partial fills, rejections. For-loop assumes instant execution.

title: Transaction Cost Modeling Commission Slippage
claim: Transaction costs: commissions (per-trade fee), slippage (market impact + latency), bid-ask spread. Accurate modeling essential; omitted costs cause backtest-to-live performance gap. Scale costs with order size and market conditions.

title: Backtest Optimism Assumptions Gap
claim: Backtests assume constant market conditions, perfect execution, no exchange outages. Reality includes regime changes, partial fills, rejections, network latency. Backtest results optimistic; paper trading crucial validation step.

title: Backtest-to-Live Gap Profit Decay
claim: Live trading diverges from backtest due to: market regime shifts, structural breaks in correlations, execution latency, liquidity constraints, regulatory changes. Profit decay (alpha decay) occurs as strategy exposures become crowded.

title: Strategy Adaptation Continuous Monitoring
claim: Continuous monitoring and adaptation required: track strategy returns vs. benchmarks, detect performance degradation, rebalance parameters periodically. Walk-forward optimization adjusts strategy without overfitting.

title: Portfolio Diversification Correlation Stress Testing
claim: Diversification across strategies (momentum + mean-reversion), asset classes (equities + futures + crypto), and time horizons reduces concentration risk. Correlation monitoring and stress testing ensure true diversification.

title: Overfitting Backtest Collapse
claim: Heavy optimization on backtest data causes overfitting; strategy fails in live trading. Symptoms: perfect Sharpe ratios, minimal drawdowns in backtest vs. immediate losses live. Requires out-of-sample validation and robustness stress testing.
